bursaulucami.name: Ulu Cami
bursaulucami.slogan: Twenty domes and a skylight over the washing fountain.
bursaulucami.line: Bayezid I ordered it after his 1396 victory at Nicopolis; its walls carry 192 calligraphy panels by 41 masters.

bursayesilcami.name: Green Mosque
bursayesilcami.slogan: Tabriz tilework glowing in green, blue and turquoise.
bursayesilcami.line: Begun in 1412 for Sultan Mehmed I, its tiles carry an inscription naming the masters of Tabriz.

bursacumalikizik.name: Cumalıkızık
bursacumalikizik.slogan: Cobbled lanes, some only 60 cm wide, and no cars.
bursacumalikizik.line: This Ottoman waqf village below Uludağ still has 270 protected houses and became UNESCO listed in 2014.

iznikhagiasophia.name: İznik Hagia Sophia
iznikhagiasophia.slogan: Where bishops once argued over icons, now a mosque.
iznikhagiasophia.line: The Second Council of Nicaea met here in 787, ending the first period of Byzantine iconoclasm.

izniklefke.name: İznik Walls & Lefke Gate
izniklefke.slogan: Walk the ring that kept Nicaea safe for centuries.
izniklefke.line: The Byzantine walls ran about 5 km, stood 10 m high and carried more than 100 towers.
